what_happened.line: The Finance Committee began FY17 departmental budget reviews with the police chief, whose requests were above the target for staff, training, equipment and capital.
The fire chief followed with above-target requests, including pay to cover EMT night shifts and to fund mandated EMT training.
The police chief held a records-system software item out of the budget and asked for two more patrol cars because the fleet is aging.
The only vote was to approve the prior minutes; no budget votes were taken.
The committee set its schedule: DPW and land use on Feb 25, library and schools on March 3, a budget hearing March 24 and votes March 31.

why_it_matters: The police and fire requests sit above the town's spending target, so they compete with other departments and could raise the town budget, mostly taxes, if they are approved at Town Meeting.
A pending police contract could move payroll further from the town manager's figure once it is settled.
watch_next: Regular meeting Feb 25 with DPW and land use, and a special meeting March 3 with library and schools.
Budget hearing March 24, then committee votes on the budget March 31.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on there being no votes and on the main presenters and deferred agenda item, but they differ in detail on the budget figures. The main thing to check is the schedule and attendance: ours lists dates through March 31 and a town manager who was absent, and the official minutes give only Feb 25 and list the town manager as present.
